questions.question: A generator converts:
options: Mechanical energy to electrical energy, using electromagnetic induction

questions.question: An emf is induced in a rotating coil because:
options: The coil heats up as it spins
The magnets slowly lose their strength
The magnetic flux through the coil keeps changing as it rotates
The brushes generate charge by friction

questions.question: The component difference between an AC generator and a DC generator is:
options: AC uses two slip rings; DC uses a split-ring commutator

questions.question: The split-ring commutator produces direct current because it:
options: Stops the coil from reversing its emf
Smooths the current to a constant value
Swaps the coil's connections to the brushes at the exact instant the emf reverses

questions.question: The motor effect is the observation that:
options: A magnet in a coil creates current
A spinning coil produces an emf
A current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field experiences a force

questions.question: A motor coil turns because its two sides:
options: Carry current in opposite directions, so they are forced in opposite directions
Are attracted to the same magnet pole

questions.question: In a DC motor, the commutator's job is to:
options: Reverse the coil current every half turn so the turning force keeps the same direction

questions.question: The relationship between a motor and a generator is that they are:
options: Completely different machines with different parts
Both powered by permanent magnets alone
The same device run in opposite energy directions

subtopics.title: Why the Grid Chose Alternating Current

questions.question: The decisive advantage of AC for a national grid is that:
options: AC is safer to touch than DC
Its voltage is easily stepped up and down by transformers

questions.question: Transmitting power at very high voltage reduces losses because:
options: The same power then needs a small current, and heat loss depends on current squared

questions.question: On a voltage-time graph, AC appears as:
options: A wave swinging between equal positive and negative maxima

questions.question: The negative half of the AC current wave represents:
options: Energy flowing back to the power station
Current flowing in the opposite direction around the circuit

questions.question: The rms value of an alternating voltage is:
options: The average of the wave over one cycle
The equivalent DC voltage that would deliver the same energy to a resistor
The voltage at the start of a cycle

questions.question: If the mains rms voltage is 220 V, the maximum voltage is 220 × √2, which equals about:
A 44 Ω heater on the 220 V mains draws an rms current of 5 A. Its average power is:
For a purely resistive AC circuit, the instantaneous power at the peak of the cycle equals:

subtopics.title: The Dynamo on the Bicycle Wheel

questions.question: A magnet resting motionless beside a coil produces:
options: No emf at all — only changing flux induces a voltage

questions.question: Pedalling becomes slightly harder when the dynamo lamp is switched on because:
options: The lamp's energy is paid for by extra work from the rider's legs

questions.question: A power station generator differs from a bicycle dynamo mainly in:
options: Scale and what spins the coil — the physics of induction is identical
Using static charge instead of coils

questions.question: Feed current into the machine and the shaft spins; spin the shaft and current comes out. These two personalities are:
The coil turns like a revolving door because:
options: Both sides are pushed the same way
The magnets alternately switch on and off
One side is pushed up and the other down, since their currents run in opposite directions

questions.question: Without the split ring's half-turn current swap, a DC motor coil would:
options: Swing half a turn and then be pushed backwards

questions.question: An electric vehicle braking while charging its battery is using its machine as:
options: A generator — the turning wheels drive the coil and produce current

questions.question: The plain average of the mains voltage wave over a full cycle is:
options: Zero — the wave is equally positive and negative

questions.question: A kettle still heats on AC because heating depends on:
options: Current squared, which is positive on both the forward and backward strokes

questions.question: The 220 V printed on appliances is:
options: The rms value — the DC-equivalent voltage for energy calculations
The peak value of the wave
A safety limit, not a real voltage

questions.question: A 2 200 W kettle on 220 V draws an rms current of 10 A. Its peak current is closest to:
